clue.text: See 12
Last of theatregoers go off to find a seat

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is the one taken

parts.note: to addle is to go rotten, as an egg goes off

explanation.surface: The final theatregoers drift out to look for a place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is the seat a rider sits on, on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Nuts, 28's local dip, roughly speaking?

indicators.note: said loosely, the phrase is only approximately the same as the answer when spoken

parts.note: Sarkozy is French, so his local swim would be in the Seine, the river through Paris

explanation.surface: Asks whether a swim in the river where the French president lives would be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is SARKOZY, the theme: a French dip is IN SEINE, which, said roughly, gives the word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for mad, crazy, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Corrects paperwork, putting top of house on in flats

indicators.note: the roof-plus-on pieces are placed inside the word for flats

parts.note: pads is slang for flats or homes
the roof is the top of a house
re means on or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone corrects documents while adding a roof to an apartment block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'flats' looks like the definition but is the outer piece, and the definition is the two-word phrase at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader checks and corrects printed text before publication, which is correcting paperwork.

clue.text: 28's food item taking seconds to secure

parts.note: to nail something is to fix or secure it

explanation.surface: A French food item taking only seconds to fasten down.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is SARKOZY, so his food is French: snails, served as escargots.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are a famous French delicacy, the escargot, so a food item a Frenchman would eat.

clue.text: Dog coats black and shine, given local food

indicators.note: the dog's name wraps around the letter for black, coating it

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to rub something is to polish it until it shines

explanation.surface: A dog with a black coat gets a polish before sharing a meal at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' here is British for one's neighbourhood pub, hence the food served there.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub grub is the plain food served in a British pub, and the local is one's regular pub.

clue.text: Mixed bag having to serve in pit, or otherwise

indicators.note: the word for serve goes inside the rearranged letters
otherwise means in another way, so the letters of pit and or are reordered

parts.note: to pour a drink is to serve it

explanation.surface: A random assortment that must be dished up in a pit or some other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; 'Mixed bag' at the front is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a miscellany, any mixed assortment, as well as a bowl of dried petals.

clue.text: See 26
Old country that is so hard to recollect

indicators.note: read as re-collect, the letters are gathered up again in a new order

parts.note: ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a former nation hard to remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recollect' rearranges IE SO HARD; it means gather again, not remember.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of the African state now called Zimbabwe, so an old country.

clue.text: Might cod be assaulted?

definitions.meaning: fish in a British chip shop is dipped in batter before frying

explanation.definitionFit: Battered means coated in batter for frying, and also violently beaten again and again.

clue.text: Where would teenagers go at night? The conclusion to mind one's business

definitions.text: Where would teenagers go at night?

indicators.note: the end letter of the next word is the one taken

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A question about teenage nightlife followed by advice to mind one's own business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a night club for dancing, a typical teenage night out.

clue.text: A hospital with a few recovered, feeding three times, no more

indicators.note: the hospital letter and the rearranged word go into the three letters like food

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for time, so three times gives three Ts
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: re-covered, the word is reworked into a new order

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A patient fed three times a day in hospital, recovered with a few others, wants nothing further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' signals the rearranging of the synonym for a few, and 'feeding' signals the container; 'no more' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: At the most means as a maximum, not more than that.

clue.text: A poet at a stretch?

parts.note: an American poet whose name, stretched out, describes a tall man

explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Henry Wadsworth Longfellow; split in two his name is a long fellow, a man drawn out to length.
explanation.definitionFit: The American poet of Hiawatha bears this surname, which also reads as a tall man.

clue.text: 28's shrug of the shoulders is Japanese when fishy sushi's starter

indicators.note: fishy means suspect or odd, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of the following word is the one taken

explanation.surface: A Japanese person shrugs when the opening course of sushi seems off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' rearranges IS JAPANESE plus S. 28 is SARKOZY, so the shrug is French: I don't know.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for I don't know is what accompanies a Gallic shrug.

clue.text: Brylcreem's horror story?

parts.note: Brylcreem is a hair cream, so a story it would tell lifts the hair, as a scary tale does

explanation.walkthrough: Brylcreem is a British hair-styling cream; a horror story is one that makes the hair stand on end.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller that makes the hair stand up with fright is called this.

clue.text: Car needing service, investing Iranian money, I treat with liquid metal

parts.note: Merc is short for a Mercedes car

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe, so the word for service wraps round the money and I

parts.note: use means service, as in of use
the rial is the currency of Iran

explanation.surface: A car going in for service, paid for with Iranian cash, gets treated with liquid metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' is the container signal, in its old sense of clothing; mercury is the metal that stays liquid at room temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To mercurialise is to treat with mercury, the metal that is liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: 28's food arrived, beginning to melt over Vicky's consort?

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: Vicky is short for Victoria, so her consort Albert shortens to Bert

explanation.surface: French food arrived and began to melt over Queen Victoria's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is SARKOZY; a French cheese. Victoria and Albert become, on familiar terms, Vicky and Bert.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft cheese from Normandy, a classic French food.

clue.text: Something painful in spreading of flu's contemptuous

indicators.note: the painful thing goes inside the rearranged letters
a spread of letters is scattered and reformed

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: Something hurtful in the way flu spreads is treated with disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading of' signals the anagram, keeping the possessive S as a letter, and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful means showing scorn, a synonym of contemptuous.

clue.text: 28's oath, the last, potentially our last

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: potentially means the letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French oath, possibly the final one we will hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges OUR LAST to UTALORS. 28 is SARKOZY, so the oath is French.
explanation.definitionFit: This French exclamation means damn it, an oath a Frenchman would utter.

clue.text: 28's stroke of genius, I produce team that's extraordinary

indicators.note: something out of the ordinary is reworked, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A manager claims a stroke of genius in producing an amazing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges I PRODUCE TEAM. 28 is SARKOZY, so the phrase is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means a master stroke, a brilliant move.

clue.text: South American cowboy awkward, replacing seat

indicators.note: one letter swaps in for another, here the final one

parts.note: gauche means socially awkward
a toilet seat is ring-shaped, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A cowboy on the pampas, ungainly when changing saddles.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for seat is loose: read it as a ring-shaped seat; it takes the place of the last E.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a horseman of the South American pampas, a cowboy.

clue.text: Just yours truly on top of bank

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: Only I am perched above the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely means only or just, nothing more.

clue.text: Wander to state capital

indicators.note: stating something means saying it out loud, so the word is heard

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Asks someone to wander off to a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a US state; it means say.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander freely without a fixed destination.

clue.text: A lovely lying back with a partner come together

indicators.note: the word lies backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means lovely
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A gorgeous person reclines with a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying back' turns GLAM into MALG.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate is to merge or unite, coming together as one.

clue.text: Breakdown of sisterly sisterhood

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The collapse of a close bond between sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' picks the answer out of sisterLY SISterhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysis is the breakdown of cells, a technical word for disintegration.

clue.text: European city, not seldom but regularly visited

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, at a steady interval

explanation.surface: A European city visited often, not rarely, but at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of NOT SELDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, a city in Europe.

clue.text: 28's dish for his members, being derogatory?

definitions.text: 28's dish for his members, being derogatory?

parts.words: 28's dish for his members, being derogatory?
parts.note: a French dish; frog is a rude name for a Frenchman, and his members are his limbs

explanation.walkthrough: 28 is SARKOZY; 'Frog' is a derogatory British name for a French person, so a Frenchman's limbs are his dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs' legs are a classic French dish, and also the limbs of a 'Frog', a slur for a Frenchman.

clue.text: 28's oath securable after negotiation

indicators.note: negotiation means working things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French curse uttered once a deal is secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after negotiation' rearranges SECURABLE. 28 is SARKOZY, so the oath is French.
explanation.definitionFit: This French exclamation is an old mild oath, literally holy blue.

clue.text: Large number touring capital almost miss the boat

indicators.note: the word for many travels around the shortened capital

parts.note: a lot is a large number

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Seoul is the capital of South Korea

explanation.surface: Many tourists, nearly at the capital, miss their boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips the last letter of the capital and 'touring' is the container signal, the large number travelling round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose out is to miss an opportunity, just as missing the boat is.

clue.text: Leader of republic bringing two islands close to monarchy

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands
Oz is a nickname for Australia, an island continent

indicators.note: close means end, so the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A republic's leader acquires two islands, bringing them near to monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island; Oz is Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Sarkozy was President of France, leader of the French Republic.
